questions.question: Why does the online path retrieve candidates before using a richer ranking model?
options: It bounds expensive feature hydration and scoring to meet the response deadline
It guarantees every catalog item is shown equally
It removes the need for a policy layer
It makes event logging unnecessary
questions.explanation: Retrieval favors recall and speed. Ranking can then spend more computation on a much smaller candidate pool.

questions.question: Which record is essential for interpreting whether a listener's click or play was a good recommendation?
options: The listener's device battery level
The full impression record, including displayed items and positions
Only the final ranker's model file
Only the track's release date
questions.explanation: An outcome has meaning only when the system knows what was shown, where it was shown, and under which model and policy decision.

questions.question: What is the safest way to use a discovery budget in a returned music slate?
options: Fill every position with unknown tracks
Add credible less-certain candidates after eligibility and relevance checks
Skip availability checks for new releases
Use the same discovery rate for every listener and surface
questions.explanation: Discovery should be controlled exposure for candidates that are still eligible and plausibly relevant in the current context.

questions.question: A model's top five results are all from the same artist. Which stage should correct this when the surface is meant to encourage exploration?
options: The playback CDN
The candidate logging job
The slate policy layer
The catalog upload service
questions.explanation: Ranking estimates item value, while slate policy applies diversity, availability, deduplication, and product constraints to the final list.

questions.question: What prevents point-in-time leakage when creating a training example for a recommendation impression?
options: Use only features that were available when the listener saw the item
Train only on popular tracks
Remove all negative feedback
Use the newest feature values at training time
questions.explanation: Future information can make offline evaluation look excellent while producing a model that cannot reproduce that quality online.

questions.question: When the online ranker times out, what must still run before returning a fallback slate?
options: A full offline retraining job
A final availability, safety, and session-deduplication policy check
A request to score the whole catalog
A new listener onboarding survey
questions.explanation: Fallbacks preserve service, but they must not bypass hard product constraints or return stale and recently played content.
